segments.arabic:
١١٨٢٩- نوبة:
خادم النبيّ ﵌ «٤»، أوردها أبو موسى في النّساء، ونسب ذلك لعبد الغني بن سعيد في المبهمات.
ذكرت في حديث زائدة، عن عاصم، عن أبي وائل، عن مسروق، عن عائشة، قالت:
(١) أسد الغابة ت (٧٣٢٧) .
(٢) في أ: في نسب الأنصار.
(٣) أسد الغابة ت (٧٣٢٩)، الاستيعاب ت (٣٥٦٠)، أعلام النساء ٥/ ١٩٥، تجريد أسماء الصحابة ٢/ ٣٠٨ الاستبصار ٤٦.
(٤) أسد الغابة ت (٧٣٣٠) .
segments.english:
11829—Nuba:
A servant of the Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace.[4] Abu Musa included her among the women and attributed this to Abd al-Ghani ibn Sa'id in al-Mubhamat.
She was mentioned in a hadith transmitted by Za'ida, from Asim, from Abu Wa'il, from Masruq, from Aisha, who said:

[1] Usd al-Ghaba, biography no. 7327.
[2] In manuscript A: “in Nasab al-Ansar.”
[3] Usd al-Ghaba, biography no. 7329; al-Isti'ab, biography no. 3560; A'lam al-Nisa', 5/195; al-Tajrid, 2/308; al-Istibsar, p. 46.
[4] Usd al-Ghaba, biography no. 7330.

segments.arabic:
مرض النبيّ ﵌ فاشتدّ مرضه فوجد من نفسه خفّة فخرج بين بريرة ونوبة «١» .
قلت: وهذا ليس بصريح في أنها امرأة، وقد وقعت في كتاب الرّدة لسيف بن عمر على ما يدلّ أنه رجل، فأخرج عن مسلمة بن نبيط، عن نعيم بن أبي هند، عن شقيق بن سلمة، عن عائشة، قالت: خرج رسول اللَّه ﵌، وقد دخل أبو بكر في الصّلاة، فأخذ عبدا يقال له نوبة وبريرة يهاديانه بينهما، فذكر الحديث.
ولكن أخرجه يعقوب بن سفيان في تاريخه، من طريق معتمر بن سليمان، عن نعيم ابن أبي هند بهذا السّند، فقال: فجاءت نوبة وبريرة فاحتملتاه ... الحديث ...
أخرجه أبو موسى أيضا من طريقه، وهو ظاهر في أنها امرأة، إذ لو كان رجلا لقال فاحتملاه.
segments.english:
The Prophet—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—fell ill, and his illness grew severe. Then he felt some relief and came out between Barira and Nuba.(1)

I say: This is not explicit that she was a woman. In Sayf ibn Umar's Kitab al-Ridda, however, it occurs in a form indicating that he was a man. He narrated from Maslama ibn Nubayt, from Nu'aym ibn Abi Hind, from Shaqiq ibn Salama, from Aisha, who said: “The Messenger of Allah—may Allah bless him and grant him peace—came out when Abu Bakr had entered into the prayer. He took with him a slave called Nuba, and Nuba and Barira supported him between them.” Then he related the hadith.

Ya'qub ibn Sufyan, however, narrated it in his history through Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman, from Nu'aym ibn Abi Hind, with this chain of transmission, wording it: “Then Nuba and Barira came and carried him…”—the hadith…

Abu Musa also narrated it through his route. It is apparent from this that Nuba was a woman, since, had Nuba been a man, he would have used the masculine dual form, “the two of them carried him.”

unresolved.explanation: The canonical Arabic, Urdu witness, and collateral Arabic entry preserve the consonantal spellings but do not supply vowels. Nuhayya and the variant Luhayya are therefore retained provisionally; their precise vocalization cannot be established from the supplied evidence.
